== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was a Church of England minister appointed to a cure in Antigua. He is named in a 1707/08 bounty list of emigrant ministers to America: "Glasgow, John, Antegoa, March 10, 1707-1708."<ref name="FMP1" /> The entry records the appointment and destination but no age, family or later life, so his birth is placed before 1707. No birthplace is recorded.

== Research Notes ==
=== Treasury warrant ===

Fothergill’s printed bounty list gives John Glasgow’s Antigua grant on 10 March 1707/8 (10 March 1708 in modern year numbering), Money Book 19, p. 200. The Treasury calendar’s March 10&15 group records a £20 passage warrant for John as chaplain to Antigua, money orders dated 11 March and a direction dated 16 March; it cites Money BookXIX pp.200, 204, Order BookVII p. 120 and Disposition BookXIX p. 118. The grouped heading does not independently assign 15 March to John. This identifies a specific financial trail for the existing 1708 event. Fothergill and the calendar abstract the same underlying warrant and are not independent family testimony. Neither gives a parent, birthplace, age, ordination or proof of arrival. The printed list and calendar were inspected; the original Treasury manuscripts were not. John remains distinct from the 1800 Trinity student and the Kilbirnie Presbyterian minister.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/listofemigrantmi00fothuoft/page/30/mode/1up Gerald Fothergill, A List of Emigrant Ministers to America, 1690–1811(1904), printed p. 30, PDF p. 38; original printed page inspected]. [https://www.british-history.ac.uk/cal-treasury-books/vol22/pp152-162 William A.Shaw, Calendar of Treasury Books 22(1952), pp.152–162, March 1708, March 10&15 entry; Money BookXIX p. 200 etc.].</ref>



The bounty defines a distinct minister appointed to an Antiguan cure, not [[Glasgow-3161|John Glasgow]], the Kilbirnie Presbyterian minister, whose settled Scottish ministry is incompatible with the appointment. Appointment does not by itself prove travel or residence.
